runners_data.name: Big Time Rascal

runners_data.name: Apple's Angel
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator naturally suited to coming late, but poor recent form (8th, 9th, 7th in last three) offers little encouragement; sim-going figures of 0W2P suggest modest ceiling on fast ground, and the race map pushes them further back than their true preference.

runners_data.name: Barnsnape Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good recently for Jim Boyle and carries strong good-ground credentials (11/15 sim-going runs), but his natural tendency to come from off the pace means he'll need to override instinct and push forward — the redistribution note is secondary to the fact he is one of the better-credentialled horses in this field.

runners_data.name: Bated Breeze
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride, which is a notable booking for a competitive yard, and three recent placed efforts show consistency; a true hold-up horse who will be pushed into midfield by the nature of this race shape, which is not where he ideally wants to be.

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with blinkered headgear who has hit the frame at 3/6f/GOO recently, suggesting course-type form exists — by nature a hold-up horse, so the crowded rear is an issue, and 0W in 15 sim-going starts tempers expectations despite the placed effort.

runners_data.name: Coiled
runners_data.note: Dropped markedly in trip from 7-8f assignments and the form figures of 9-8-8-5 tell a consistent story of not getting competitive; a genuine hold-up runner who is squeezed further toward the rear by the cluster of similar types, with no wins from 15 good-ground runs.

runners_data.name: Manhattan Chute
runners_data.note: Returning from 61 days off with 0W in 15 sim-going runs and a sequence of 8th-9th-9th-9th on similar tracks — this race is a tall order, and stepping up to 6f after a series of 5f efforts adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Mishy's Star
runners_data.note: Carries the "fades in finish" flag alongside blinkered headgear, and the recent form of 9th and 14th over 8f suggests a drop to 6f is an attempt to unlock latent speed; natural hold-up tendencies are problematic in this shape, and the 24-day break on 2/12 sim-going form offers little.

runners_data.name: Molly Marine
runners_data.note: 68 days off the track for Jack Jones's yard (2/15 T14) is a concern, and just 1 run from 6 on similar going with no wins or places tells its own story — a natural hold-up operator whose redistribution into midfield compounds a difficult task on return.

runners_data.name: Poet
runners_data.note: Carries the "fades in finish" flag, is rated lowest in the field at OR 38, and the last five finishes read 7-9-10-9-9 — 0W in 15 good-ground runs with a proven pattern of not quickening; his natural hold-up style is the least advantageous in this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends out a runner with an excellent 10/47 14-day record, and crucially Port Hedland has won at 6f on Good at a similar venue — a patient hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace quickens late and there is a lane to close.

runners_data.name: Some Nightmare
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with consistent placed form in the 3-5 range and a preference for 5f, stepping up to 6f with a hood; the recent good and firm form figures are respectable and he's a horse who races handily without always being a pure hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby has a 2/25 T14 record and Jason Watson is a strong jockey booking — a 2nd and two 4ths in recent good-ground form at 6-7f marks Valsharah as one of the more consistent horses in this OR 50 band, and he shapes as a natural mover forward from the hold-up cluster.

races.paceDynamic: Big Time Rascal is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field, and with no other genuine pace-setter to pressure them, they are likely to dictate a comfortable, controlled tempo down the Brighton straight on Good to Firm ground. The remainder of the field is almost entirely composed of hold-up types, meaning the race shape is essentially one horse on the lead with a pack of closers tracking at various distances behind. With a sustainable, uncontested gallop, the advantage sits firmly with horses that can travel prominently in behind the leader and strike from second or third gear — pure hold-up finishers will need an exceptional late run to bridge the gap if the pace is never truly honest. The field holds far more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Barnsnape Boy, Molly Marine, Bated Breeze, and Valsharah are the most likely to push forward and secure a prominent berth in behind Big Time Rascal despite their natural style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Big Time Rascal bowls along uncontested and sets a comfortable gallop that suits a well-timed prominent challenge.
scenarios.body: Big Time Rascal controls fractions from the front while the chasing pack jostles for position, leaving the nearest travellers in behind ideally placed to challenge over the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Movers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If one or two hold-up horses successfully push up to race prominently and use that position to overhaul the leader in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Horses like Valsharah or Barnsnape Boy, hustled forward to race in the first three, track Big Time Rascal's easy pace and deliver a sustained challenge inside the final two furlongs; their good-ground form makes them dangerous in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Big Time Rascal sets a stronger-than-expected pace and the prominent horses are drawn into a flat-out gallop that leaves them vulnerable late.
scenarios.body: A faster tempo would compress the race and open a late lane for genuine hold-up horses, with Port Hedland — a course winner who is comfortable coming from off the pace on good ground — best positioned to exploit any late fade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early gallop causes a mid-race concertina with a large group arriving at the furlong pole together.
scenarios.body: A messy finish with horses bumping and checking suits the luckiest draw rather than the classiest runner, though Valsharah's recent placed form on this type of ground gives them an edge in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Big Time Rascal's ability to secure an uncontested lead is the critical variable — if any horse pushes forward aggressively from the gates to challenge, the whole pace dynamic unravels.

Valsharah and Barnsnape Boy will both attempt to race more prominently than their natural style dictates; if they clash for position in the first furlong, the resulting shuffle could compromise both horses' chances.
Port Hedland's Tony Carroll yard has a strong 10/47 14-day strike rate — monitor market moves for this horse as a dangerous hold-up type with a proven win at this distance on Good ground.

The bunching of 11 hold-up horses in a 13-runner field means draw and early positioning will be unusually influential — horses drawn centrally who can ease into a midfield berth without traffic are structurally advantaged.

Some Nightmare is stepping up from 5f to 6f wearing a hood — watch how he handles the extra furlong; if he gets a strong-paced last two furlongs his 5f speed may not last, but in a slowly-run race he could be better placed than expected.

runners_data.name: Parading

runners_data.name: Radahn
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter; George Scott runner stepping up to 7f after a debut second at Sandown (OR 120), with Benoit De La Sayette booked and conditions ideal — his ability to dictate terms unanswered is the dominant factor in this race.

runners_data.name: Telegraphic

runners_data.name: Better Nature
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby takes over on this Jonathan Portman filly who has form over today's trip (3rd, 7f Good) and handles the going; a genuine hold-up type who needs the pace to be honest enough to set up her late effort, which is not guaranteed with Radahn likely to control proceedings.

runners_data.name: Alice Rocks
runners_data.note: Form figures of 5-9 across two starts on Good ground and a Soft track offer little encouragement; a true hold-up type whose natural position is at the rear, mapped forward here only because of the quantity of closers in the field — Jason Watson will have limited options to improve her poor finishing record.

runners_data.name: Serenity Bay
runners_data.note: The least experienced runner (one run, 11th on Good) and flagged for a tendency to fade in the finish — a concern over 7f on Good to Firm; Ed Dunlop sends her out after a 50-day break and Saffie Osborne will need significant improvement to be competitive from a hold-up position.

races.paceDynamic: Radahn is the only confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push him early, he should be able to stride to the front and control the tempo on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's undulating 7f. The hold-up contingent — Better Nature, Serenity Bay, Parading, and Alice Rocks — will be deployed from midfield to rear, though Parading and Alice Rocks are natural hold-up types redistributed forward on the map because the field contains more closers than the race shape has room to accommodate at the back. With Radahn setting a measured, uncontested gallop from the front and a clutch of hold-up horses tracking in behind, the race shape is most likely to produce a pace-controlled contest that will suit a horse capable of travelling prominently or picking up efficiently from just off the pace — patient closers with a strong late run will be chasing a potentially well-conserved leader into the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Radahn Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Radahn dictates an unchallenged tempo and is never headed, his class advantage (OR 120) and fresh conditions allow him to steal the race from the front.
scenarios.body: Radahn sets a sustainable pace on the Good to Firm ground, with Benoit De La Sayette nursing him through the undulations before kicking clear inside the final 2f; the hold-up horses simply have too much ground to make up against a well-rated, uncontested leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Nails It
scenarios.trigger: If Radahn's gallop proves just quick enough to flatten the field but Radahn himself ties up late, a strong finisher swoops.
scenarios.body: Better Nature or Telegraphic, tracking from midfield, picks up the pieces in the final furlong as the leader runs out of steam on the climb; Brighton's finish can expose a horse that has given too much too early, though Radahn's class makes this a secondary scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling just behind Radahn in the early stages sustains a challenge from 2f out and outstays him.
scenarios.body: Telegraphic, lightly raced and unknown in terms of ceiling, looms as the likeliest horse to latch onto Radahn's coattails and simply prove the superior individual over 7f; George Scott's yard has maintained good strike rate (T14: 3/20) which supports Radahn's own chance in this shape too.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the field finishes in a heap, allowing true closers to grab late positions.
scenarios.body: This depends on Serenity Bay, Alice Rocks, or Parading producing finishing bursts from out the back, but all three are lightly experienced or flagged with finishing concerns, and Parading and Alice Rocks are not naturally suited to this shape in any case; the probability is low because the pace architecture simply does not set up a true end-to-end gallop.

watchPoints.text: Radahn — monitor whether Benoit De La Sayette allows him to bowl along unchallenged from the gate; if he secures a clear lead by the 5f pole, his rivals' task becomes very difficult.
Telegraphic — lightly raced and unquantified, David Egan may attempt to sit just behind Radahn and pounce late; any signs of greenness or traffic trouble early would be the key risk to this plan.

Better Nature — Rob Hornby needs a strong enough pace to set up a meaningful late run; watch whether she travels fluently in behind or gets detached, as that will determine whether she can land a blow in the final furlong.

Parading and Alice Rocks — both true hold-up types pushed forward on the race map; if either ends up further back than their mapped position suggests, their chance of finishing in the money is materially reduced given the likely moderate tempo set by a lone front-runner.
Going confirmed as Good to Firm for the 6:50 — faster than the headline "Good" implies; any runner whose best form has come on softer ground should be noted as potentially disadvantaged.

runners_data.name: Dalmally

runners_data.note: Returned an unusual mid-race fall (F) last time and hasn't won at anything from 7 runs; Seamus Cronin (5lb claimer) takes the ride and the horse needs to improve considerably from a hold-up role to factor — 49 days off adds a small unknown.

runners_data.name: Romanovich

runners_data.name: Rainbow Sorbet

races.paceDynamic: Dion Baker is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to push him, he should stride into an uncontested lead from the gates and set a honest but manageable tempo over Brighton's undulating 7f. Kondratiev Wave is the only other horse with legitimate prominent credentials and may track Dion Baker in second, but the field behind is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types who will have to wait for gaps on this tight, turning track. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get their natural rear position — Romanovich, Prefer The Sister, Rainbow Sorbet, and My Boy Jack are the most credible finishers from the back but will be competing for the same ground in the straight. With a solo leader controlling a measured tempo on good-to-firm ground, this race shape strongly favours the horse closest to the pace at the top of the straight — a prominent or tracking style that can sustain into the final furlong without needing a gap to appear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dion Baker Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dion Baker breaks cleanly and bowls into an uncontested lead, dictating every yard from the front.
scenarios.body: He sets a comfortable gallop, avoids interference, and Brighton's undulating track allows a well-placed leader to sap the finishing kick of hold-up types who face a wall of horses rounding home. His recent 7f Brighton form (three wins in five) and good-to-firm affinity make him the standout beneficiary of this exact shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Runs Dion Baker Down
scenarios.trigger: If Kondratiev Wave or a prominently-placed rival sits tight to Dion Baker's quarters and outpaces him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A sustained pace with one horse hunting the leader throughout leaves the hold-up brigade too far back on a track that rarely rewards deep closers, but the tracker gains on every stride once Dion Baker flattens out. Kondratiev Wave's consistent placed form at 7f and good-to-firm gives him the credentials to land this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Carve Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Dion Baker's lead evaporates quickly enough to bunch the field and create a wall for late closers to thread through.
scenarios.body: Romanovich, Prefer The Sister, or My Boy Jack would need a clear run to arrive in time, and Brighton's short home straight makes threading late moves genuinely difficult. These are true hold-up types forced wide or into traffic, meaning any late surge carries significant execution risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Interference
scenarios.trigger: If there is trouble in running, scrimmaging for position as multiple hold-up types compete for the same tracking ground around the final bend.
scenarios.body: With so many horses of similar OR clustered tightly in the hold-up bracket, a messy race with interference in the straight could randomise the finish and benefit whichever runner escapes cleanest. My Boy Jack or Mighty Ruler could emerge beneficiaries purely through finding daylight rather than on form merit.

watchPoints.text: Dion Baker — if he breaks slowly or misses the kick, there is no second front-runner to set the pace and the race could collapse into an untidy crawl that brings closers back into play.

Romanovich, Prefer The Sister, Rainbow Sorbet and My Boy Jack — four genuine hold-up types will funnel into the same ground turning for home at Brighton, raising a real risk of interference or checked runs in the straight; any traffic incident here reshapes the result.

Kondratiev Wave — 39 days since last run and stepping back in trip slightly; if he is not sharp enough to track Dion Baker from the off he loses his primary tactical advantage on this pace-dominated map.

Mighty Ruler — the fall in last run (F) is unexplained and the horse's profile is hard to read fully; watch the betting market and paddock for signs of any physical issue before drawing conclusions on his chance.

Going confirmation — declared as Good To Firm throughout Brighton's card; any softening toward Good would marginally reduce Dion Baker's advantage and help the hold-up horses who have placed on softer surfaces.

races.paceDynamic: Super Hit is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride into an uncontested, sustainable gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Brighton. The pace will be controlled and moderate — Super Hit dictates the tempo, the field strings out behind, and the race becomes a test of stamina and finishing kick rather than raw speed. The field contains a heavy density of hold-up types — Pershalla, Gone Rogue, Annexation, and Voix De Bocelli are all natural closers who cannot all settle in their preferred rear position and have been redistributed to midfield in the map; of these, Gone Rogue and Annexation are likeliest to push forward and secure the more prominent midfield slots. A controlled, single-pace front-runner scenario on quick ground over a distance that stretches stamina most benefits hold-up horses who can travel through the race and pick off a tiring leader, though the compression of so many closers behind the same sectionals means finding clear daylight in the straight becomes critical.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Super Hit Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit is allowed to roll along at a comfortable, unforced gallop and controls every sectional without pressure.
scenarios.body: Super Hit exploits the uncontested lead to conserve energy, setting a pace that suits its own stamina profile and leaving the closers with minimal margin to reel it in; on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Brighton, a front-runner allowed to dictate without being stretched can prove very hard to catch.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If Super Hit's pace proves just quick enough to string the field out but fades inside the final two furlongs, leaving the race open for finishers.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop compresses the hold-up pack through the middle stages, and when Super Hit's effort flattens out approaching the final furlong the closers arrive in a bunch; Bownder and Boubyan, natural hold-up types with form at similar trips on Good ground, are positioned to capitalise with late runs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Super Hit at close quarters — rather than coming from deep — picks the perfect moment to challenge and overwhelms the leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Gone Rogue has prominent-race form and has been pushed forward in the map, meaning it could shadow Super Hit and deliver a sharp challenge in the straight; Annexation's recent second at 1m2f on Good shows it can finish well from close range.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grinds Out
scenarios.trigger: If pace quickens significantly from halfway and turns the race into a genuine stamina slog, exhausting early movers and exposing fitness differences.
scenarios.body: Pershalla and Boubyan, both effective over 1m2f+ on Good going in their recent histories, would benefit from a thorough test that rewards proven staying power over tactical speed; however, with so many redistributed hold-up types unable to get their natural position, execution risk is high.

watchPoints.text: Super Hit's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the race-defining factor — watch whether Christian Howarth settles it or allows the pace to quicken mid-race, as either choice reshapes every other runner's scenario.

Gone Rogue and Annexation, both redistributed from hold-up to midfield, could end up racing in an awkward no-man's-land — watch how Tom Queally and Jack Doughty position them in the early stages as it will determine whether they are a threat or a non-factor.

Boubyan returns from a 64-day break wearing headgear for the first time at this yard — fitness and hood effect are both unknowns that could see it either bolt up fresh or fade tamely if the run comes too soon.

With five of seven runners compressed into a midfield/hold-up cluster, the straight at Brighton narrows and finding a clear passage late will be crucial — a wide draw or a well-timed split could prove decisive for Bownder and Pershalla especially.

races.paceDynamic: This is a field of eight confirmed hold-up horses at Brighton's 1m2f trip, meaning there is no genuine front-runner to set the fractions — the race will almost certainly crawl into the straight before erupting into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs on the undulating switchback track. Without a pace-setter to stretch the field, the tempo will be dictated by whoever is most reluctant to give ground, and on good-to-firm ground at Brighton, the tactical race will compress the field and make position off the bend absolutely critical. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Mist Of Time, Bear Steps, Dogged, Launceston, All About George, and Outrace are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield simply because the rear is overpopulated, meaning only one or two will genuinely achieve a tracking position. In a race with no natural leader, the horse best able to win a sprint finish from mid-division — with a jockey sharp enough to find daylight on Brighton's tricky camber — holds the clearest tactical advantage; Myna's recent course-distance form and Graffiti's placings at this trip make them the profiles most naturally suited to what this race shape will produce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Compressed Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no horse assumes the lead willingly and the field crawls for the first mile before a mass sprint erupts in the straight
scenarios.body: The race bunches throughout and turns into a two-furlong dash up the Brighton hill, rewarding horses with the sharpest finishing kick and jockeys best at finding room on a tricky camber

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Solo Breakaway Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If one runner — most likely Graffiti or Myna — forces the pace from halfway to steal a march on a flat-footed field
scenarios.body: The horse that moves first through the turn for home gains a decisive few lengths on a field ill-equipped to respond, with the sprint-finish types caught out of position on the final climb

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-to-Back Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace causes the field to fan wide on the bend and a hard-pressed mid-race move strings the field out
scenarios.body: Horses with the highest recent form at 10-12 furlongs on good ground are isolated from the pack and grind out a winning advantage before the finish line; Myna's winning run at 10f good and Dogged's placed record at 10f good are the relevant benchmarks here

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Caught Flat
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so sedate that the field never truly separates and fatigued finishers are caught flat as the trip stretches stamina reserves
scenarios.body: Horses who have faded in the finish — Mist Of Time, All About George, and Outrace are all tagged as finishers who fade — are most exposed, and the benefit accrues to the single runner with both a sprint finish and superior recent form

watchPoints.text: Myna is the horse to track throughout — if David Egan positions it close enough to the camber rail entering the straight, its recent 10f good-ground win gives it a tangible form edge over this field in a sprint finish

Bear Steps and Mist Of Time are both three-year-olds stepping up to 12f for the first time with no stamina evidence; if the race develops any sort of sustained gallop after halfway, watch for both to drop away sharply before the final furlong

Graffiti's tongue-tie and blinkers combination suggests a horse that has needed headgear to focus — if it misses the break or gets caught wide on the final bend, the gear advantage is nullified before it matters

With no confirmed front-runner in the field, watch the first two furlongs closely — whoever is pushed to the front by a reluctant field effectively becomes the accidental pace-setter and may get first run on the field turning for home, a significant advantage at Brighton's sharp track

runners_data.name: Rory Rocket
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good at Brighton last time (1/6f/GOO) and has winning form on similar ground; hold-up style suits a pace-set race well, and apprentice Jude Fernandes's 7lb claim gives a weight advantage worth respecting — the Brighton course form is a material positive here.

runners_data.name: Too Darn Good
runners_data.note: Henry Candy three-year-old who has placed at 3/5f/GOO most recently and wears headgear; Rob Hornby is a strong booking but the form string (36-673) shows inconsistency, and a 0W record from 9 similar-going runs tempers expectations despite the competitive profile.

runners_data.name: Kento
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old is the race's only natural front-runner and will get a soft lead by default; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) signals he is operating slightly outside his optimal role, but his record of 1W4P from 15 similar-going outings and last-eight run of 135123 shows he is in good order — the concern is whether a pedestrian pace gives the closers an easy target.

runners_data.name: Faustus
runners_data.note: Veteran of eight years, Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claim) takes the ride; wearing headgear and running just five days after his last start, this is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural finish from deep is constrained in a small field — his redistribution to midfield on the map reflects that he cannot physically sit last of five and still generate the momentum his style requires.

runners_data.name: Honour Your Dreams
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater's six-year-old has placed twice from 15 similar-going runs (0W1P) and wears a tongue-tie; Alistair Rawlinson rides and the horse's true deep-closing style is compressed by the small field size, similar to Faustus — recent form of 824429 shows limited reliability, and a 15-day absence adds a small fitness question mark.

races.paceDynamic: Kento is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field and, with no genuine pace rival to press him, should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Brighton's 5½f. The remainder of the field — Rory Rocket, Too Darn Good, Faustus, and Honour Your Dreams — are all hold-up types by inclination, meaning Kento inherits an uncontested lead by default rather than by superiority. Faustus and Honour Your Dreams are genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply nowhere for a queue of hold-up horses to sit at the back in a five-runner field; their true finishing style remains rear-to-midfield sweeping, not prominent. This race shape — a single, unchallenged leader setting a measured tempo — classically favours hold-up horses who can close into a steadily run sprint, giving Rory Rocket and Too Darn Good the most natural finishing profile if they can get into position early enough.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kento Controls, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kento bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but not scorching pace, leaving closers to reel him in from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: Kento's uncontested lead at a moderate tempo sets up a straight sprint finish where the hold-up horses get a clean run at him; on Good to Firm ground the pace is unlikely to be slow enough to completely stop them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Kento Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Kento's controlled front-running proves decisive and the closers cannot peg him back on good-to-firm ground down Brighton's straight.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner dictating every yard of a 5½f sprint on fast ground can build an unassailable lead if the pursuing pack fails to coordinate their challenge early enough; Kento's recent form (135123) shows he fires fresh and has the tactical speed to make it stick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a strong late run for the deepest-sitting closers.
scenarios.body: Faustus and Honour Your Dreams would need Kento to go off far too quickly for his own good, which is unlikely given the absence of rivals to force his hand; their redistributed positions on the map reflect that this scenario depends on horses racing against their natural instincts in a small field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Any Can Win
scenarios.trigger: If the field fails to settle into a coherent shape and multiple horses jostle for position in the opening furlong.
scenarios.body: An unusually unsettled early dynamic in a small sprint field can compress the finish and randomise the outcome; with all non-Kento runners carrying hold-up tendencies, any positional confusion would most likely benefit whoever gets the clearest passage to the outside rail.

watchPoints.text: Rory Rocket has direct Brighton course form (1/6f/GOO) and a 7lb claiming jockey — watch if Fernandes positions closer than the hold-up tag suggests, as that would move him into the ideal seat just off Kento's pace.

Kento's STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) means he is not in his natural lead-from-the-front groove; if David Egan misjudges the tempo and crawls, he risks gifting the closers an easy target at the foot of the hill.

Faustus runs just five days after his last outing — watch market moves to gauge whether connections believe the quick turnaround is a sign of confidence or necessity, as a below-par effort at this age on short rest is plausible.

With four hold-up types chasing one front-runner, watch the first furlong for positional traffic — if Rory Rocket or Too Darn Good are slow away and get trapped wide or behind, their chance of delivering a late run down the straight is significantly reduced.

Good to Firm ground (confirmed in the going report for the 8:50) will ensure the surface plays fast — horses who act on quick ground and have done so recently (Kento, Rory Rocket) hold a meaningful edge over those with more modest similar-going records.
